ZinOperatorAlgebra.Purpose: Zin operators are closed and compiler-defined. Operator overloading is forbidden. Every compound-assignment form evaluates its destination exactly once.

ArbitraryWidth.Rule: iN is two's-complement and represents exactly -2^(N-1) through 2^(N-1)-1.
@sizeOf(T) equals ceil(@bitSizeOf(T)/8) for standalone arbitrary-width integers.
packed aggregates use exactly N bits for an iN/uN field.
No implicit integer promotion changes the declared bit width.

Arithmetic.Rule: Wrapping and saturating are alternative overflow policies for one arithmetic operation and are not combined with each other.

Bitwise.Rule: Bitwise operations operate on the exact bit width of the integer type and never numerically overflow.

CountPolicy.Checked: For T with width W, a shift count n must satisfy 0 <= n < W. A constant invalid count is ZIN-E4012. A runtime invalid count traps in safe modes.
CountPolicy.Wrapping: The effective count is n mod W. Examples: <<%, >>% and their assignment forms.

ResultPolicy.Checked: Left shift is checked for value loss in comptime and safe modes. Unsigned right shift is logical. Signed right shift is arithmetic. Right shift itself cannot overflow numerically.
ResultPolicy.Saturating: For left shift, overflow saturates to the destination type's numeric bound. The count policy remains independent. Thus <<| and <<%| are distinct.

ShiftCombine.Description: Zin additionally supports shift-combine operators. A combine operator applies a normal arithmetic or bitwise combiner to the original left operand and its shifted value. This gives compact, explicit bit-manipulation without operator overloading or hidden calls.

PrefixForm.Lowering: tmp_a = evaluate(a) // exactly once tmp_b = evaluate(b) // exactly once shifted = SHIFT(tmp_a, tmp_b) result = COMBINER(tmp_a, shifted)

SuffixForm.Lowering: tmp_a = evaluate(a) // exactly once tmp_b = evaluate(b) // exactly once shifted = SHIFT(tmp_a, tmp_b) result = COMBINER(shifted, tmp_a)

ShiftCombine.Canonicalization: Prefix and suffix forms are both legal. For commutative combiners they produce the same numeric value, but both spellings remain defined so operator composition is mechanically complete.
ShiftCombine.AssignmentRule: Appending '=' to any valid shift or shift-combine token creates its compound-assignment form. The destination is evaluated exactly once, then replaced by the operator result.

Disambiguation.Rule: `>>|` is the suffix OR-shift-combine token because right shift has no saturating-result form.

CompoundAssignment.Rule: For any valid binary operator OP declared compound-assignable, `lhs OP= rhs` is semantically `lhs = lhs OP rhs` except lhs is evaluated exactly once.
Compound assignment does not introduce an implicit cast that the corresponding assignment would reject.
A compound assignment to a moved, immutable, non-addressable, or otherwise invalid destination is a compile error.

ComptimeAndSafety.Rule: All operator semantics are identical at comptime and runtime except that a statically known violation is a compile error rather than a runtime trap.
ReleaseFast may remove safety checks but may not change wrapping, saturating, bitwise, or explicitly wrapping shift-count semantics.
